subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Increasing the number of channel and carrier proteins in a membrane would increase the rate of facilitated diffusion only if:
options: the temperature is reduced to zero
the molecules are non-polar and small
there is still a concentration gradient and proteins were previously the limiting factor
questions.explain: More transport proteins raise the rate only when proteins limit it and a gradient remains to drive the movement.

questions.q: The fluid-mosaic model describes the cell membrane as:
options: a continuous protein sheet with no lipid
a fluid phospholipid bilayer with proteins embedded in a mosaic pattern
a rigid layer of protein sandwiched between lipid
questions.explain: The model depicts a fluid bilayer in which proteins are scattered like a mosaic and can move laterally within the membrane.
Two successive divisions yield four haploid cells, each genetically unique due to crossing over and independent assortment.

questions.q: Self-antigens normally do not trigger an immune response because:
options: They are too small to be detected
Lymphocytes that would respond to the body's own antigens are destroyed or suppressed during development
questions.explain: During development, lymphocytes complementary to self-antigens undergo clonal deletion or suppression, preventing autoimmune attack.

questions.q: Receiving an injection of antibodies (e.g. anti-tetanus serum) provides:
questions.explain: Ready-made antibodies are introduced artificially without the body making its own, giving immediate but short-lived (passive) protection.

questions.q: A plant cell becomes plasmolysed when placed in a concentrated salt solution because:
options: water leaves the cell by osmosis, so the protoplast shrinks away from the cell wall
salt is actively pumped out of the cell
water enters the cell, pushing the membrane against the wall
questions.explain: The external solution has a lower (more negative) water potential, so water leaves the cell and the plasma membrane pulls away from the wall.

questions.q: In the cell-mediated response, T-helper cells are activated when they:
options: Bind to antigens presented on the surface of an antigen-presenting cell
Bind directly to free antigens in the blood
questions.explain: T-helper cells have receptors complementary to antigens displayed by antigen-presenting cells, and this binding activates them.

questions.q: In plant cells, water potential is determined by the equation:
options: Psi = solute potential x pressure potential
questions.explain: Water potential equals the (negative) solute potential plus the (usually positive) pressure potential exerted by the cell wall.

questions.q: In the co-transport of glucose in the ileum, glucose is absorbed into the epithelial cell because:
options: a sodium-glucose co-transporter carries glucose in alongside Na+ moving down its gradient
glucose diffuses freely through the phospholipid bilayer
glucose is pumped directly by ATP into the cell
glucose is actively pumped out of the cell
questions.explain: Na+ entering down its gradient (maintained by the Na+/K+ pump) drives glucose into the cell against its gradient via the co-transporter.

questions.q: Antibodies passed from mother to baby in breast milk give the baby:
questions.explain: The antibodies are received naturally (via milk/placenta) and the baby does not make them itself, so it is natural passive immunity.

questions.q: A cell measures 30 mm in a photomicrograph taken at a magnification of x1500. The actual size of the cell is:
questions.explain: Actual size = image size / magnification = 30 mm / 1500 = 0.02 mm = 20 micrometres.

questions.q: A key structural difference between a prokaryotic and a eukaryotic cell is that prokaryotes:
options: always have a cellulose cell wall
lack a true nucleus and have a single circular DNA molecule in the cytoplasm
possess membrane-bound organelles and a nucleus
questions.explain: Prokaryotes have no nucleus or membrane-bound organelles; their circular DNA lies free in the cytoplasm and ribosomes are smaller (70S).
